content:
A clip of David Letterman sharply criticising media executives for purging late-night talk show hosts who criticise Trump — along with his insights on what this represents — resurfaced on Monday after the president barred White House reporters from briefing.

The late-night talk show legend, speaking at The Atlantic Festival 2025, opened by warning that under an autocratic government and autocratic rule, "sooner or later, everyone will be affected."

Letterman referenced CBS's decision to cancel his successor Stephen Colbert's The Late Show, attributing it to Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison not wanting to "trouble" Trump.

He then brought up ABC's suspension of Jimmy Kimmel's show after Brendan Carr, the pro-Trump TV czar, threatened consequences against the network and its affiliates if they did not act on Kimmel's comments about the killing of Charlie Kirk — comments that had also become a focus of right-wing criticism.

Letterman said: "We can all see where this is going, right? This is media being manipulated."

"That's bad, that's childish, that's ridiculous. You can't be firing people all over town because you're afraid of or want to curry favour with the autocrat — the criminal — in the Oval Office. That's not the way it's supposed to work."

The clip went viral again on social media after former Labor Secretary Robert Reich posted about it.

He wrote: "This warning David Letterman gave about the media a year ago sounds unfortunately just as relevant today."

"He was right: you can't appease a tyrant."
